review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new definition is `seeleyAffineMap x₀ r x = x₀ + r • x`. It is a named specialisation of a translation composed with a scaling. It is not a competing version of `AffineMap.homothety`, which has a different orientation and centre convention. The file implements it with Mathlib's `MeasurableEquiv.addLeft`, `measurableEmbedding_const_smul₀`, `Measure.map_addHaar_smul` and `fderiv_comp_smul`, so it reuses the existing API. Its uses are almost entirely inside this file (one external use in SobolevPoincareBall.lean). I did not find a practical cost from duplication. `euclideanBall`, `classicalGradient` and `Vec` are defined in other files of the library (Cutoff/Ball.lean and Cutoff/Basic.lean), not in this one. Any question about whether they duplicate Mathlib concepts such as `Metric.ball` or `EuclideanSpace` belongs to those files. The remaining declarations are scaling and change-of-variables lemmas, which are outside this rubric. The main uncertainty is that I did not examine those other files in depth.
